newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cifra seen launching 1.6 bln new shares.
newsitem.headline: Cifra seen launching 1.6 bln new shares.

text.p: Mexican retail giant Cifra will launch 1.6 billion new A and B shares following the recent joint venture agreement with U.S. firm Wal-Mart, analysts said on Friday.
Wal-Mart moved earlier this week to acquire a controlling interest in its joint venture with the Mexican retailer via a $1.2 billion deal.

"The book value will allow 1.6 billion shares to be issued for Wal-Mart," said one analyst after a shareholder meeting organized by Cifra. The agreement will translate into a dilution of Cifra's share capital, he added.
The issue is aimed at maintaining an equilibrium of 51 percent in A and 49 percent in B shares, both of which have controlling power, the analyst said.
The total number of Cifra shares will rise to around 4.8 billion, he added.

Analysts who took part in the meeting, called to explain the agreement with Wal-Mart, said that with this issue and after a public offering the U.S. firm will be able to consolidate 50 percent of its global operation under the control of Wal-Mart Stores Inc.
The percentage of ordinary series A and B shares is currently 38 and 37 percent respectively. This will shift to 42 and 41 percent, while series C will slip from 25 to 17 percent, the analyst said.

As a first step in this process, Cifra will pay a dividend of 0.75 pesos per share, equivalent to 2.4 billion pesos for each of the 3.2 million shares already issued, he added. ((--Karina Balderas, Mexico City newsroom 525 72895 62))
